expectations.text: End users prevented from granting consent to third-party OAuth applications — consent by an authorised administrator only (ISM-2137)
expectations.evidence: "Disable user consent by default... forces every new integration through a governed approval path" with admin consent workflow — substance of ISM-2137 (ID not cited)

expectations.text: OAuth application consents reviewed at least every six months, revoking unused apps and excessive permissions (ISM-2138)
expectations.evidence: Review cadence given only as "a defined cadence (e.g., quarterly)"; the ISM's at-least-six-monthly requirement (ISM-2138) is not stated

expectations.text: Central logging of consent grants, token issuance and token use (ISM-2139)
expectations.evidence: Logs "capturing OAuth consent grants" into SIEM mentioned, but central logging of token issuance and token use (ISM-2139) is omitted

expectations.text: OAuth device code flow disabled unless required; where required, restricted to authorised accounts and managed devices (ISM-2140)
expectations.evidence: OAuth device code flow (ISM-2140) is never mentioned

expectations.text: Frames why: consent phishing and token theft are current attack paths; ties to session/token binding and revocation controls in the same release
expectations.evidence: Mentions consent phishing ("illicit consent grant attacks") but no token-theft framing tied to session/token binding and revocation controls in the same release
